test_title: PYST 61: SSC CGL 2024 - General Knowledge (Held On 17 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In which of the following years was the Election Commission of India founded?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1950**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Election Commission of India (ECI) was established on **25th January 1950**.
 
• It is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• The ECI ensures the conduct of free and fair elections in the country, which is a fundamental aspect of the democratic framework of India.
 
• The Election Commission operates under the authority of the Constitution per Article 324, and subsequently enacted Representation of the People Acts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI)**

 
 
• The ECI is responsible for the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to Parliament and to the Legislature of every State and of elections to the offices of President and Vice President held under the Constitution.
 
• The body administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies in India, and the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.
 
• It was originally a one-member body but was made a three-member body in 1989.
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) heads the Election Commission of India.
 
 
 
• **Article 324 of the Indian Constitution**
 
 
• Article 324 vests the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections in an independent body, which is the Election Commission.
 
• The Election Commission has the power to take all necessary steps to ensure free and fair elections.
 
 
 
• **Representation of the People Acts**
 
 
• The Representation of the People Act, 1950 provides for the allocation of seats in the House of the People and in the Legislative Assemblies, the delimitation of constituencies for elections, the qualifications of voters at such elections, and other related matters.
 
• The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides for the actual conduct of elections in India, the qualifications and disqualifications for membership of Parliament and State Legislatures, and the resolution of election disputes.
